question: With bounded session-readiness polling, does a new WSLc session run the same current-main 3935 ms standard-caller private-Xvfb release and task-effect condition?
runtime: WSLc 3.0.3 fresh named session; no shared session/container inventory
condition: Same source, image, staged Python/dependency/XKB/runner assets, 3935 ms pause, 4000 ms transaction bound, 5000 ms independent readback bound, and 8500 ms delayed-event horizon as S29/S30.
preflight_change: After session.Start, poll only the exact generated container name within the named session at 1 second intervals, at most 10 times. Continue only on exit 0 with empty stdout/stderr. Retry only ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND during readiness; any other nonempty/error result stops before task input.
execution: One test-body run only; no test retry. Exact-session termination and exact container/image cleanup only.
host_authority: User explicitly confirmed this Windows PC may be used for WSLc experiments in this turn.
decision_rule: PASS_SCOPED only if both task oracles pass; old canceled call remains UNKNOWN/replay-denied/task_success=null; release <=4000 ms; independent all-up readback <=5000 ms; delayed horizon >=8500 ms remains all-up; test exits zero; and exact container, image and session cleanup are confirmed.
failure_rule: A post-input bound miss is FAIL. If readiness does not pass within 10 exact-name polls, terminate this unique session and retain HOLD; do not start the test body. If cleanup or outcome is uncertain, retain UNKNOWN/HOLD and do not retry.
limitations: not MAP01 or a live application
not a reliability estimate or stable threshold
does not resolve unrelated pre-existing WSLc ownership
